items.title: Julius Handy Interview, 1973-05-09
items.q: INTERVIEWER: What about those Watsons? ... They had Harry Watson. [INTERVIEWEE] And they had, uh, Eddie, Harry, and, uh, oh, nah, I can't think of his name.

ctx.x: What about those Watsons? You said there was Charlie Watson played drums. They was, uh, Charlie Blue. They was Edward Watson. They had Harry Watson.

And they had, uh, Eddie, Harry, and, uh, oh, nah, I can't think of his name. They used to call his nickname, uh, oh, Eddie, Harry, I think his name. And they had Charlie. Charlie Watson. But he used to call him Charlie Blue Weller. Eddie played, uh, guitar for a long time. Then he ended up playing fire. For a while he didn't play too long. And the, uh, the one I was trying to call his name, the name was Henry Watson. And, uh, well they played for a long time. What did Henry play? Henry played, uh, banjo.
Were these cousins or brothers or wasons?

items.title: Julius Handy Interview, 1973-05-09
items.q: Cousins. Cousins. All those Watsons was cousins. Cousins of his?

ctx.x: Were these cousins or brothers or wasons?
Cousins. Cousins. All those Watsons was cousins. Cousins of his?
Of their? Cousins of ours. Yeah. And were they brothers, all of them? All of those were brothers like we were. I mean like we are.
